newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Who's Who of Indonesia involved in gold drama.
newsitem.headline: Who's Who of Indonesia involved in gold drama.

text.p: A long-running wrangle over one of the world's richest gold finds involves a virtual Who's Who of Indonesian business and politics.

At the center of the dispute is the spectacular Busang gold deposit, which is located in a rugged jungle area of Indonesia's East Kalimantan province on Borneo Island and is believed to contain at least 57 million ounces of gold, currently worth over $21 billion.

The rush for the gold has drawn in an assortment of Indonesian heavyweights, led by President Suharto and his family, U.S.-educated businessman and politician Jusuf Merukh, and billionaire timber tycoon and Suharto golfing partner Muhammad "Bob" Hasan.

A resolution appeared closer on Friday when the Indonesian government said it "understood" a proposal from the drama's two main protagonists -- Canadian mining companies Barrick Gold Corp and Bre-X Minerals Ltd -- to carve up the site.
Topping the list of players is Suharto, the 75-year-old former army general who has ruled the sprawling archipelago for the last 30 years and will be the final judge of who wins and loses.
Two members of his immediate family are also involved: eldest son Sigit Harjojudanto, 45, and eldest daughter Siti Hardiyanti Rukmana, 47.
Bre-X, which found the deposit, announced last October that Sigit's Panutan Duta group would act as a consultant to the mining firm after it ran into a dispute with Jusuf Merukh.

Merukh, a former legislator with the minority Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) and supporter of its ousted leader Megawati Sukarnoputri, claimed ownership of 40 percent of the entire Busang find, a claim dismissed by Bre-X.
Bre-X offered Sigit's company $1 million per month for 40 months and a cut in the Busang stake in return for its services.
Canada's Barrick Gold Corp has teamed up with Suharto's eldest daughter Rukmana, whose Citra Lamtoro Gung group is involved in toll roads and broadcasting.
Rukmana, known as Tutut, who also plays a prominent role in the ruling Golkar party, appears often at her father's side in public since the death of Suharto's wife of 49 years in April.
The sons of two government ministers are also linked to Barrick.

Also involved is Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana, 60, a retired military lieutenant-general from the holiday island of Bali. He was a member of the elite strategic reserve (Kostrad) founded by Suharto.

This week Merukh's company PT Krueng Gasui, which owns an undisputed 10 percent of the first of the Busang find's three blocks, launched a C$2 billion ($1.48 billion) lawsuit in Canada to gain the larger stake which he claims.
The suit also names businessman Syakerani and his son Ahmad Yani, whose family controls PT Askatindo Karya Mineral, which owns 10 percent interest in the motherlode.
In another twist, Syakerani said he had sold a stake in PT Askatindo to timber baron Hasan who is involved in a web of companies involving everything from plywood and cement to airlines.
An ethnic Chinese and convert to Islam, Hasan plays golf with Suharto regularly every week.
